blurbs.text: Abram built an altar here on first entering Canaan, and a generation later his grandson Jacob dreamed of a ladder to heaven and named the place the house of God.
After the kingdom split, Jeroboam set up a golden calf shrine here to rival the temple at Jerusalem.
Once the Jebusite stronghold of Jebus, the city became Israel's capital after David's conquest and the site of Solomon's temple, until Babylon burned it in 586 BC.
Rebuilt after the exile as the Second Temple city, Jerusalem was the setting for Jesus' final week, his crucifixion and resurrection, and the birth of the church.
Jerusalem's story runs from a Canaanite hill fort through the City of David, two temples, and the birth of the church.
Abraham pitched his tents at Mamre near Hebron and bought a field here to bury Sarah; his son Isaac and grandson Jacob were later buried in the same cave.
David was anointed king here and reigned from Hebron for seven years before capturing Jerusalem.
Egypt sheltered Abram in famine and later Joseph's family; his descendants multiplied there for centuries before Moses led them out in the Exodus.
The infant Jesus found refuge in Egypt from Herod's soldiers before his family returned to settle in Nazareth.
Egypt's story in scripture runs from Abram's famine refuge and Joseph's rise to power, through the Exodus centuries later, to briefly sheltering the infant Jesus.
Abram's family paused here on the way from Ur, and a generation later his grandson Jacob fled here to escape Esau and work for his uncle Laban.
Abram built his first altar in Canaan near Shechem's oak, and Jacob later bought land and dug a well here, burying his household's foreign idols under the same oak.
Joshua renewed Israel's covenant here at the end of his life, and Joseph's bones, carried up from Egypt, were finally buried in the ground Jacob had bought.
Israel crossed the Jordan into Canaan here and won their first battle when the city's walls fell, the opening victory of the conquest.
Abraham and Isaac both dug wells and swore covenants of peace here, giving Beersheba its name; Jacob departed from here for Haran and, decades later, for Egypt.
Jesus' friends Mary, Martha, and Lazarus made their home here on the Mount of Olives' eastern slope, and it became his lodging place in his final week before the crucifixion.
Founded by Asshur out of Nimrod's kingdom of Babel, Nineveh grew into one of the great cities of the ancient Near East.
Jonah reluctantly preached God's coming judgment to this "exceeding great city," and its people repented at his warning.
After the Danites conquered and resettled the old Canaanite town of Laish, Jeroboam later set up a golden calf shrine here to rival Jerusalem's temple.
Paul appealed to Caesar and was brought here under guard, where he spent his final recorded years awaiting trial while still preaching under house arrest.
Believers scattered by persecution planted a church here whose members were first called "Christians," and it became the sending base for Paul's missionary journeys.
Omri built his new capital on a hill he bought from Shemer, and it remained the northern kingdom's royal city until Assyria besieged and took it, exiling Israel.
After Stephen's martyrdom scattered the believers, Philip preached the gospel here, and the Samaritans received the Holy Spirit through the apostles.
Israel's tabernacle stood here for centuries after the conquest, the nation's central place of worship before Jerusalem's temple was built.
Jesus left Nazareth to make this fishing town on the Sea of Galilee his ministry base, teaching in its synagogue and healing many who were brought to him.
The persecutor Saul was struck blind by a vision of the risen Christ on the road here, and emerged days later to preach in the same city's synagogues.
Nimrod's kingdom began at Babel, where the builders of a great tower were scattered when God confused their language.
Jerusalem's exiles wept by Babylon's rivers, remembering the city they had lost, until the kingdom itself fell to the Medes and Persians.
Cyrus of Persia decreed that the exiles could return home and rebuild the LORD's house in Jerusalem.
